JUDGMENT Heard Shri T. A. Mirza, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the appellant-State.
None for the respondents, though served.

2. The present appeal arises out of the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandrapur, dated 23.11.2001 in Regular Criminal Case No. 326/1999, by which the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate acquitted the respondents herein for the offence punishable sections 7(i) read with Section 2(ia)(a) punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) and Section 7(i) read with Section 2(ia)(m) punishable under Section 16(i)(a)(i) read with Section 17 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act of 1954" for the sake of brevity) and Rules made thereunder.
3 APPEAL214.02.odt 3.
The facts giving rise to the present appeal, in short, are as under :
The complainant Jagdish Khushal Kamble, (PW1) was appointed as a Food Inspector in the year 1972.

When he was discharging his duties as Food Inspector at Chandrapur, on 21.1.1999, he along with Naresh Bhagwat Goswami (PW4) visited the premises of M/s Suhas Food Products situated at E-79, M.I.D.C., Chandrapur,
respondent no.1 was present in the factory.

The complainant Shri Kamble (PW1)
disclosed his identity to him and shown his inclination to draw samples of food articles for the purpose of testing and analysis.
He inspected the premises and drawn Inspection Report (Exh.22).
During the inspection, he found 100 packed identical packets of pasteurized and homogenized cow milk and pasteurized and homogenized double tonned milk.
Each packet was of one liter.
He selected one packet of both milk for the purpose of sample.

He demanded 750 ml each quality of milk from the State Of Maharashtra vs Watan S/O Bhayyaji Kokas & 5 Others on 26 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141175911/
2 respondent no.1.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the said was given to the complainant in two different clean, dry and empty containers.
He paid the cost of the samples and obtained receipt from the respondent no.1 (Exh.23).
He also prepared the notice as 4 APPEAL214.02.odt contemplated under Section 14-A of the Act of 1954 and handed over the same to the respondent no.1.
He thereafter divided the samples equally in three clean, dry and empty bottles and also added 20 drops of Formalin as preservative in each sample bottle.
Those were sealed by him.

He, thereafter sent the packet to the Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory,
Nagpur.
He also gave an intimation as required under the Act of 1954 through the Legal Health Authority.
The report of the Public Analyst dated 03.3.1999 (Exh.39) was received and as per the report, the sample was not in conformity with the standard as per the Rules framed under the Act of 1954.

4. As per the prosecution case, thereafter, the Local Health Authority and Assistant Commissioner for Food and Drug Administration, forwarded his proposal with all relevant documents to the Joint Commissioner of Food and Drug Administration at Nagpur on 29.4.1999 (Exh.45).
After obtaining consent, the complaint was lodged in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandrapur.

sentences.text: 5 APPEAL214.02.odt 5.
The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandrapur framed the Charge against the respondents in Regular Criminal Case No. 326 of 1999 under Exh.52.
In order to bring home the guilt of the respondents, the complainant examined in all four witnesses.

They are (1) Jagdish Khushal Kamble (P.W.1), the complainant. ; (2) Ashok Purushottam Choudhary, Assistant Commissioner, F.D.A.,
Chandrapur, who received the proposal from the Food Inspector (PW1) and as per his claim, gave a letter dated 08.7.1999 to the respondents for exercising their right under Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 ; (3) Prakash Narayan Shende, Drug Inspector, Yavatmal ; and (4) Naresh Bhagwat Goswami, a panch witness, in whose presence PW1 obtained samples from the respondent no.1.
6.

The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, after appreciating the evidence as brought on record, on the touch stone of Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954, found that indefeasible right has been violated and only on that count, he acquitted the respondents.
7. To test whether the judgment of acquittal can stand to the scrutiny of law, the relevant provision will have to be looked into.

6 APPEAL214.02.odt Sub-section 2 of Section 13 of the Act, reads as under :
"13. Report of Public Analyst :- (1) ......
(2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other State Of Maharashtra vs Watan S/O Bhayyaji Kokas & 5 Others on 26 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141175911/
3 particulars have been disclosed under section 14-A forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired,
either or both of them may make an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory."
8.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Municipal Council, Delhi .vs. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970] has ruled that a right conferred by Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 to the accused is indefeasible and valuable right since the Certificate of the Director of Central Laboratory supersedes the report of the Public Analyst and has to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents.

entities.text: Municipal Council, Delhi .vs. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7 APPEAL214.02.odt 9.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ghisa Ram's case cited supra, it has to be seen whether the opportunity was given to the respondents to exercise their valuable right.
The document at Exh.49 is the communication given by P.W.2 Shri Choudhary to the respondents.

Perusal of Exh.49 shows that the report of the Public Analyst, Nagpur along with Exh.49 was given to the respondents for exercising their right under Section 13(2) of the Act for sending the same to the Central Laboratory at Calcutta.
10. The complainant in his cross-examination has stated that the acknowledgment or receipt of Exh.49 by the respondents is not on record.
His evidence shows that, that part is concerned with the Public Health Authority.

11. P.W.3 Prakash Shende, the Drug Inspector of Food and Drug Administration has stated in his evidence that he had not give notice to the respondents for getting the sample tested from Calcutta Laboratory.
12. Thus, we will have to fall back on the evidence of P.W.2 8 APPEAL214.02.odt Ashok Choudhary to see as to whether the report was sent to the respondents/accused.

13. Though, the prosecution tries to rely on Exhs.76 to 81 as the acknowledgment by the respondents, in that behalf, with the assistance of the learned Additional Public Prosecutor when I perused Exhs.76 to 81, even the learned Additional Public Prosecutor was unable to point out that it bears signature of the respondents.

It appears that since the signatures of the respondents were not appearing on Exhs.76 to 81, therefore, that cannot be treated as an evidence appearing against the respondents and therefore, it appears that the said was not put to the respondents/accused when they were examined under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

14. In my view, the learned Judge of the Court below, therefore, rightly found that the valuable right of the respondents to get the sample re-analyzed by the Central Laboratory at Calcutta is violated.

There is nothing on record by way of cogent evidence to show that the respondents were in receipt of State Of Maharashtra vs Watan S/O Bhayyaji Kokas & 5 Others on 26 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141175911/
4

sentences.text: Public Analyst's report and in spite of that, they failed to exercise their right.
It was the duty 9 APPEAL214.02.odt of the prosecution to prove and to dispel all doubts in respect of serving the report of Public Analyst upon the respondents.

15. In this case, in my view, the learned Judge of the Court below has rightly found that the prosecution has failed to discharge the said burden and therefore, in my view, has rightly acquitted the respondents.
16. In that view of the matter, the criminal appeal fails and the same is dismissed.
